questions.prompt: h(x) = 2^x + x - 5 is continuous and increasing, so h(x) = 0 has exactly one solution. h(1.715) ≈ -0.002 and h(1.725) ≈ 0.031. What can be concluded?
questions.prompt_markup: h(x) = 2^x + x - 5 is continuous and increasing, so h(x) = 0 has exactly one solution. h(1.715) ≈ -0.002 and h(1.725) ≈ 0.031. What can be concluded?

choices.text: The solution is strictly between 1.715 and 1.725, so it rounds to 1.72 to two decimal places.
Nothing can be concluded about the solution, because neither h(1.715) nor h(1.725) is exactly 0.
The solution is exactly 1.72, because 1.72 is halfway between 1.715 and 1.725.
The solution could round to 1.73, because h(1.725) is positive and 1.725 rounds up to 1.73.

questions.correct_answer: The solution is strictly between 1.715 and 1.725, so it rounds to 1.72 to two decimal places.
questions.grading_note: The sign change brackets the root inside the rounding interval [1.715, 1.725) (strictly inside, so no tie). The others claim exactness, misread the bracket, or ignore the sign change.

questions.skill: Compare an approximation with an exact logarithmic solution
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: 2^x = x + 2 has the exact solution x = 2 (2² = 4 = 2 + 2) and a second, negative solution. Why is the negative solution found by approximation, while 2^x = 4 is solved exactly?
questions.prompt_markup: 2^x = x + 2 has the exact solution x = 2 (2² = 4 = 2 + 2) and a second, negative solution. Why is the negative solution found by approximation, while 2^x = 4 is solved exactly?

choices.text: Negative numbers cannot be exact solutions of an exponential equation, so any negative solution of 2^x = x + 2 must be approximated, while x = 2 is exact.
The negative solution is approximated because 2^x is negative for x < 0, so logarithms cannot be taken of it; 2^x = 4 has a positive power, so x = log₂ 4 = 2.

2^x = 4 isolates the power, so x = log₂ 4 = 2; in 2^x = x + 2 the variable is both in an exponent and outside it, and no algebra step isolates it, so the negative solution (about -1.69) is approximated.
Approximation is needed only because x = 2 is already a solution: once one exact solution is known, the other solution of the equation cannot also be found exactly.

questions.correct_answer: 2^x = 4 isolates the power, so x = log₂ 4 = 2; in 2^x = x + 2 the variable is both in an exponent and outside it, and no algebra step isolates it, so the negative solution (about -1.69) is approximated.
questions.grading_note: Equations that mix exponential and linear terms usually have no algebraic solution, even when one root (here x = 2) can be found by inspection. The others make false claims (2^x > 0 for all x).
